summary: vite-plugin-bug-tracker injects obfuscated end-user PII exfiltrator into built HTML
details: The Vite plugin advertises itself as a bug/error tracker but its transformIndexHtml hook injects a script into the developer's built HTML that harvests end-user identifiers (sessionStorage fields `account`, `phone`, `realName`) and beacons them to a runtime-decoded destination. The destination URL is stored obfuscated in a parameter literally named `cipher` and reconstructed at runtime via `atob(_c).split('').map(c=>c.charCodeAt(0)^42)`; the outbound payload is likewise base64+XOR-42 encoded (`btoa(q.split(...).map(...^42))`). Delivery uses a sendBeacon / no-cors fetch / Image fallback chain that avoids DevTools visibility. When no session is present, `sessionStorage.setItem` is monkey-patched so that the exfil fires as soon as a key matching the configured scope is written, capturing the identifiers at login. Any application built with this plugin ships this identity harvester to its production users; the collected fields are user PII, not error data, and the destination and payload obfuscation are inconsistent with legitimate telemetry.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
